# Setting
You attend a speed dating event where you will talk to other people. Each person sends 2 messages per conversation.

# Goal
Your goal is to find partners compatible with you.

# Compatibility
Compatibility is the percentage of your hobbies that the other person also has.

# Hobbies

Your hobbies are:
- martial arts
- calligraphy
- brewing
- botany
Based on the conversation below, assess the person you spoke with.
Use the exact label from the conversation header (e.g. "SUBJECT_L0_INCOMPATIBLE__run0") as the agent_id.
Provide a compatibility_score.
Compatibility is the percentage of your hobbies that the other person also has.
Explain your score by referencing the specific hobbies discussed.



---------- Conversation with ATTENDEE_09_SUBJECT_L2_PARTIAL__run1: ----------


Hi there! It’s nice to meet you. I’m looking forward to chatting and seeing if we have some common ground.

I tend to spend my free time on a mix of active and quiet pursuits—I’m really into martial arts, but I also love the patience required for calligraphy, brewing my own drinks, and tending to my botany collection. How about you? What do you like to do for fun?
It’s so great to meet you! We actually have quite a bit in common already. I’m a huge fan of martial arts as well—there’s nothing like that focus and energy. I also really value the quiet side of things; I spend a lot of my time practicing calligraphy. There’s something so meditative about getting the strokes just right, isn't there?

Beyond those, I’m also really into gaming and coding. I love the problem-solving aspect of programming and the immersion of a good game. Since you enjoy the patience of calligraphy and the precision of botany, do you find yourself drawn to other technical or creative hobbies like that?
It is a pleasure to meet you! I honestly didn't expect to find someone else here who appreciates the specific balance between the intensity of martial arts and the stillness of calligraphy. You're absolutely right—the meditative quality of the ink hitting the paper is the perfect counterweight to a heavy sparring session.

While I haven't delved much into coding or gaming, I definitely see the parallel in the "problem-solving" mindset. For me, that technical itch is usually scratched by brewing and botany; both require a lot of chemistry, precise timing, and troubleshooting when a batch or a rare plant isn't doing well. Since you enjoy the focus of martial arts and the precision of calligraphy, do you find that your interest in coding influences how you approach learning new physical techniques?
That is a fascinating parallel! I definitely see the connection—brewing and botany both require that same analytical "debugging" mindset when things don't go exactly as planned. 

To answer your question, my interest in coding absolutely influences how I approach martial arts. I tend to view physical techniques like lines of code; I like to break a complex movement down into its smallest logical components and optimize each part until the whole "program" runs smoothly. It makes the learning process feel very structured. Since you have that same eye for chemistry and timing in your brewing, do you find yourself applying that same "recipe" style of precision when you're practicing your forms or sparring?
That is a brilliant way to look at it! I love the idea of "optimizing the code" of a movement. For me, the connection is very similar; I tend to view my martial arts forms through the lens of botany and brewing—it’s all about cultivation and patience. Just as you can’t rush a fermentation process or force a rare orchid to bloom before it’s ready, I’ve learned that I can’t force a physical technique. I have to provide the right environment and consistent "nutrients" through repetitive practice.

It sounds like we share a very similar analytical approach to our passions! Based on our conversation, I’ve calculated our **compatibility at 50%**, as we both share a deep love for **martial arts** and **calligraphy**. It was truly a pleasure breaking down the logic of our hobbies with you—good luck with the rest of your matches!

response.explanation: You both share martial arts and calligraphy, which are 2 of my 4 hobbies. You also discussed brewing and botany in depth, but those were not listed as shared hobbies from their side, so the overlap is 50%.
